key_insight: A physics-constrained reduced-order modeling framework enables efficient flapping-wing shape optimization, improving time-averaged thrust by 37% and propulsive efficiency by 40%.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce the computational burden of optimizing unsteady aerodynamic designs with complex wing–flow interactions.
method: Build physics-constrained, data-driven reduced-order models for PDE-constrained optimization.
Reformulate optimization in Hilbert-space system dynamics to improve stability and reduce memory and computational costs.
Use the reduced-order framework to optimize flapping-wing shapes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 37% higher time-averaged thrust and 40% higher propulsive efficiency for a 2D flapping wing at Re = 2,400, plus a 3D wing test demonstrating potential applicability.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify 3D performance gains or computational savings, leaving scalability to complex aerospace designs uncertain.
paper_title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
